title: Coherent formal modules are closed under binary products
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. For any two coherent adic inverse systems [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], the vertex of every limiting binary product cone in the ambient category of inverse systems of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is again a coherent adic inverse system.

source.place: Section 0EHN and Lemma 087X, binary-sum argument written out

proof.text: Construct H_n = F_n ⊞ G_n with diagonal transition maps and its projection cone. Biprod.lift applied componentwise is natural, and biprod.hom_ext proves that this cone is a limit.
Apply the binary-sum clause of Scheme.Modules.isCoherent_kernel_cokernel_biprod_and_submodule at each level to obtain coherence of H_n.

Apply formalModuleQuotient_factor with equal powers to each biproduct projection. Both composites of the ideal-product inclusion with the projections vanish because the corresponding ideal products of F_n and G_n are zero. Biprod.hom_ext makes the inclusion zero; as an image inclusion it is monic, so IsZero.of_mono_eq_zero makes its source zero.

Bundle formalModuleQuotientMap at a fixed exponent as a functor using formalModuleQuotientMap_id and formalModuleQuotientMap_comp. Cancel the cokernel projection to prove this functor additive. Mathlib preservesFiniteBiproductsOfAdditive and preservesBinaryBiproducts_of_preservesBinaryProducts give mapBiprod. Compose its canonical isomorphism with biprod.mapIso of the two given quotient-transition isomorphisms. Cokernel.π_desc and the two transition equalities verify the required projection composite, after biprod.hom_ext.

Replace the arbitrary discrete binary diagram by its canonical pair through diagramIsoPair and LimitPresentation.changeDiag. The constructed limit and the given limit have isomorphic vertices; coherentFormalModules_of_iso transports the three conditions to the given vertex.
